approvedTerms.definition: A Git repository: its files, commits, branches, and tags, together with its issues, pull requests, and releases.
approvedTerms.notes: Use "repo" only in URLs, command names, and space-constrained labels.

approvedTerms.definition: A named line of commits in a repository. The default branch is the one a clone checks out.
A recorded change to a repository, identified by its hash.
Your own copy of a repository under your account. Change it freely and open pull requests back to the original.
Download a repository with Git, for example git clone https://forkmesh.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY.
A tracked bug report, task, or request in a repository.
A proposal to merge commits from one branch or fork into another, with its discussion, checks, and reviews.
approvedTerms.notes: "PR" is acceptable in compact labels and CLI output; spell it out in sentences.

approvedTerms.definition: An approval, a request for changes, or comments on a pull request.
A complete copy of a repository on another host that stays in sync and can serve clones when the source is offline.
The first push that fills a new mirror from an existing copy. After seeding, the mirror keeps itself in sync.
A person the repository owner trusts to merge, release, and change settings. Their signed actions are accepted by every mirror.
A computer that serves repositories: your own machine, a server you run, or a ForkMesh-managed host.
The ForkMesh desktop application. Say "desktop app (Qt)" only where build instructions need the toolkit.

protocolTerms.explanation: A running copy of ForkMesh (desktop app, server, or phone) that signs and syncs on behalf of an account.
The ForkMesh web service that routes requests to healthy mirrors. It is not the canonical Git store.
The signed list of branch and tag commits a mirror must match before it can serve a repository.
A host's signature over the branch and tag commits it serves.
Commit history: each commit points at its parents.
How signed issue and pull request events merge into one current state without conflicts.
A short-lived claim that stops two hosts from processing the same issue or pull request at once.
The queue of signed events waiting to be delivered to other hosts.
An encrypted copy of a private repository that a host stores without being able to read it.
Sharing repository activity with the fediverse (Mastodon and other ActivityPub servers).

discouragedTerms.reason: ForkMesh uses the GitHub-style name for proposed changes; the /pulls route and API already say pull.
Approving a pull request is a review.
The promise is independent hosts and mirrors; peer-to-peer suggests file sharing and hides Git workflows.
Qt is the UI toolkit, not a product name users recognize.
Delegate is protocol jargon from other decentralized forges.
Seed is the first push into a mirror; the copy itself is a mirror.
Users choose hosts and mirrors; the mesh is an implementation detail.
